examples.en: Oh no, I left my wallet at home.
Oh no, today was the deadline!

examples.ko: 아뿔싸! 하고 외쳤을 때는 이미 늦었어요.
examples.en: By the time I cried out 'Oh no!', it was already too late.
Oh no, I forgot to bring my phone charger.
Oh no, I got on the bus going the wrong way.

examples.ko: 문을 닫고 나서야 아뿔싸, 열쇠가 안에 있다는 걸 알았어요.
examples.en: Only after closing the door did I realize, oh no, the key was inside.

explain: 실수나 잘못을 방금 깨닫고 후회할 때 혼잣말처럼 해요. 말투가 조금 예스럽고 이야기 속 느낌이 있어서, 가볍게 말할 때는 '아차'나 '앗'도 써요.

phrases.en: Oops, I left my umbrella behind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍게 실수를 깨달았을 때 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in daily speech when you notice a small mistake.

phrases.en: Oh no, I missed the bus!
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 놀라거나 당황했을 때 나오는 짧은 소리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short sound you make when suddenly startled or flustered.

phrases.example: 열쇠를 두고 나온 걸 알고 '아뿔싸' 하고 깨달았어요.
phrases.en: I realized I had left my key behind and thought, 'Oh no.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기하듯 말하거나 글로 쓸 때 어울리는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits storytelling or writing.

explain_en: Realizing a mistake too late, slightly dated or literary tone. You say it like a mutter the moment you realize a mistake and regret it. It sounds a bit old-fashioned and storylike, so in casual talk people also use '아차' or '앗'.

examples.en: Whoa, I almost missed my step.
Oof, I didn't know it was this heavy.
Oops, I spilled the coffee!
Whoa, you startle me when you come out so suddenly!

examples.ko: 어이쿠, 정말 미안해요, 앞을 못 봤어요.
examples.en: Oops, I'm so sorry, I didn't see you.
Goodness, it's already this late.

explain: 깜짝 놀랐을 때, 실수했을 때, 몸이 아프거나 힘들 때 나오는 소리예요. 비슷한 소리로 '아이쿠', '어이구'가 있어요. 말투가 조금 정겹고 가벼워서 일상 대화에서 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: Ouch, I bumped my head.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어이쿠'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used a lot with almost the same meaning as 어이쿠.

phrases.en: Oh my, I'm too tired to walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들거나 기가 막힐 때 나오는 소리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sound made when tired or exasperated.

phrases.en: Whoa, you startled me! You were there?
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 놀랐을 때 뒤에 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Added after the sound when something suddenly startles you.

explain_en: Reaction to a slip, pain or near accident (어이쿠, 넘어질 뻔했다) This is the sound people make when startled, when they make a mistake, or when something hurts or is tiring. Similar sounds are '아이쿠' and '어이구'. The tone is a little warm and light, so it fits everyday conversation.

examples.en: I can't stand bugs.
My younger sibling can't stand spicy food.
My father really hates being late.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 신발이 젖는 건 질색이에요.
examples.en: I hate it when my shoes get wet on rainy days.
I hate cleaning, but I have to do it today.
My friend can't stand lies, so my friend is always honest.

explain: '싫어하다'보다 훨씬 강하게, 보기만 해도 몸이 움츠러들 정도로 싫을 때 써요. 보통 '~라면 질색이다'나 '~(은/는) 질색이다'처럼 말해요. 가볍게 말하는 구어에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I absolutely can't stand cockroaches.
phrases.nuance_ko: '딱'을 붙이면 정말 싫다는 느낌이 더 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 딱 makes the feeling of dislike even stronger.

phrases.en: My younger sibling hates shots with a passion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '질색'에 '하다'를 붙여, 싫어하는 모습을 동작처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attaches 하다 to the noun, describing the dislike like an action.

phrases.en: What I can't stand is loud noise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '질색인'이 뒤의 말을 꾸며서, 정말 싫은 대상을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier 질색인 describes something one truly can't stand.

explain_en: Spoken; strong personal aversion to something (벌레라면 질색) It is much stronger than '싫어하다': you recoil just at the thought of something. People usually say '~라면 질색이다' or '~(은/는) 질색이다'. It comes up often in casual speech.

en: to complain; to grumble; to whine

examples.en: My younger brother grumbles that there are no side dishes.
The child whined for me to buy a toy.
Please don't keep complaining that it's hard.
If I whine to my mom, I feel a bit better.
He worked while grumbling that his pay was low.
The way she whined like a spoiled child was cute.

explain: '불평하다'와 달리, 가까운 사람에게 어리광을 부리듯 불만을 늘어놓는 느낌이에요. 실제 대화에서는 '투정을 부리다'라는 말도 많이 해요.

phrases.example: 아이가 밥을 먹기 싫다고 투정을 부려요.
phrases.en: The child grumbles that he doesn't want to eat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '투정하다'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때 더 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '투정하다', and heard more often in speech.
phrases.en_equiv: to throw a fit; to grumble

phrases.example: 동생이 매일 반찬 투정을 해서 엄마가 힘들어하세요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling complains about side dishes every day, so Mom gets tired.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹을 것에 대해 불만을 말하는 투정이에요. '밥투정'도 같은 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Complaining about food. '밥투정' is used the same way.

phrases.en: Please don't grumble about the hot weather.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그만하라고 말할 때 쓰는 부정 명령이에요. 친구나 가족에게는 '투정하지 마'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command telling someone to stop. With friends or family, say '투정하지 마'.

explain_en: Childlike fussing about food or gifts; spoken, often to family. Unlike '불평하다' (to complain), it feels like airing grievances to someone close in a childish, spoiled way. In real conversation people also often say '투정을 부리다'.

t90.ax: The child whined for me to buy a toy.

examples.en: Gasp, I didn't bring my wallet!

examples.ko: 뒤에서 소리가 나서 헉 하고 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A sound came from behind and I gasped in shock.
Whoa, it's already ten o'clock?

examples.ko: 계단을 뛰어 올라오느라 헉 숨이 찼어요.
examples.en: I ran up the stairs and was out of breath.
I gasped when I saw the price.

examples.ko: 친구가 헉 하는 소리를 내며 뒤로 물러섰어요.
examples.en: My friend made a gasping sound and stepped back.

explain: 갑자기 놀라거나 숨이 찰 때 나오는 소리예요. 문자나 메신저에서 '헉'이라고만 보내도 놀랐다는 뜻이 돼요. 비슷한 '헐'은 어이없거나 놀랄 때, '아'는 깨달았을 때 써서 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.example: 갑자기 큰 소리가 나서 헉 하고 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: I gasped in shock when there was a sudden loud noise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀란 모습을 '헉 하고'로 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how someone was startled.

phrases.en: Whoa, really? The exam is tomorrow?
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀란 마음을 먼저 말하고 질문을 이어 가는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows surprise first, then leads into a question.

phrases.example: 계단을 뛰어 올라와서 헉헉 숨이 차요.
phrases.en: I ran up the stairs and I'm out of breath, panting.
phrases.nuance_ko: '헉'은 한 번 놀라는 소리이고, '헉헉'은 힘들어서 계속 숨 쉬는 소리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: '헉' is a single gasp of surprise; '헉헉' is the sound of continued heavy breathing.

explain_en: It is the sound you make when startled or out of breath. In texts a bare 헉 means you are shocked. 헐 is similar but leans toward disbelief, and 아 is for sudden understanding, so the feelings differ.

examples.en: Um, where did you put that, you know, book?
I met what's-his-name yesterday. What was his name again?

examples.ko: 거시기가 뭔지 알죠? 그거 좀 가져다주세요.
examples.en: You know that thing, right? Please bring it over.
Oh, you know, that person.
It's a bit of an awkward topic, so it's hard to say.
When my grandmother gets stuck for words, she says 'geosigi'.

explain: 이름이 갑자기 기억나지 않거나 바로 말하기 곤란할 때 사람, 물건, 일을 대신 가리키는 말이에요. 말투가 편하고 구어체라서 발표나 면접 같은 격식 있는 자리에서는 쓰지 않아요. '그거', '그 뭐더라'와 비슷하게 쓰여요.

phrases.example: 거시기 있잖아요, 어제 만난 그 사람 이름이 뭐였죠?
phrases.en: You know, what was the name of the person we met yesterday?
phrases.nuance_ko: 말을 시작하며 생각이 안 나는 것을 대신할 때 쓰는 편한 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to start a sentence when you can't recall the word.

phrases.example: 그 뭐더라, 어제 말한 영화 제목이 생각이 안 나요.
phrases.en: What was it again... I can't remember the title of the movie you mentioned yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거시기'보다 조금 덜 사투리 같고 누구나 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds a bit less dialect-like than 거시기 and anyone can use it casually.

phrases.en: Please bring me that thing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모르는 이름 대신 쓸 수 있는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic word to use in place of a name you don't know.

explain_en: It stands in for a person, thing or matter when you suddenly can't recall the name or find it awkward to say directly. It is casual and spoken, so avoid it in formal settings like presentations or interviews. It works much like '그거' or '그 뭐더라'.

examples.ko: 차를 정비 업체에 맡기고 나서 소음이 거짓말처럼 사라졌어요.
examples.en: After I left the car with a repair shop, the noise vanished as if by magic.
After I took the medicine, my headache disappeared like magic.
Unbelievably, the sky cleared up.

examples.ko: 시험 전날 막히던 문제가 거짓말처럼 풀렸어요.
examples.en: The problem I was stuck on the day before the exam got solved just like that.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 거짓말처럼 하루아침에 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: That shop shut down overnight, as if it were unreal.
It may sound like a lie, but it's all true.

explain: 믿기 어려울 만큼 갑자기, 완전히 변하거나 사라질 때 써요. 뒤에는 '사라지다, 낫다, 풀리다' 같은 말이 잘 어울려요. 좋은 일이든 나쁜 일이든 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: My aching back got better as if by magic.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거짓말처럼'과 뜻이 거의 같고, 말할 때는 '같이'도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly identical in meaning to '거짓말처럼'; '같이' is also common in speech.

phrases.en: Winning the lottery is unbelievable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사가 아니라 '일'을 꾸며서 믿기 힘든 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Instead of an adverb, this modifies a noun to describe something hard to believe.

phrases.en: The problem I was worried about got solved like magic.
phrases.nuance_ko: '풀리다'와 함께 쓰면 어려운 일이나 걱정이 갑자기 해결된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '풀리다', it means a difficulty or worry is suddenly resolved.
phrases.en_equiv: to be resolved as if by magic

explain_en: Use it when something changes or disappears so suddenly and completely that it is hard to believe. It goes well with verbs like 사라지다, 낫다 and 풀리다, and works for good or bad events.

examples.ko: 거참, 그 사람 말 한번 이상하게 하네요.
examples.en: Well, that person talks in a strange way.
Goodness, why is the weather like this all of a sudden?

examples.ko: 거참, 일이 이렇게 꼬일 줄은 몰랐어요.
examples.en: Dear me, I didn't expect things to get this tangled.
Wow, that's amazing. How did you know?

examples.ko: 거참, 말도 안 되는 일이 다 있네요.
examples.en: Gosh, there are all sorts of absurd things happening.

examples.ko: 거참, 어쩔 수 없죠. 일단 기다려 봐요.
examples.en: Well, it can't be helped. Let's wait for now.

explain: 어이없거나 못마땅하거나 신기할 때 혼잣말처럼 먼저 나오는 말이에요. 구어에서 많이 쓰고 글에서는 거의 안 써요. 윗사람에게 쓰면 버릇없이 들릴 수 있어서 친한 사이나 혼잣말로 써요.

phrases.en: Well now, what should I do?
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤란하거나 난처할 때 혼잣말처럼 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said like a mutter when you are troubled or at a loss.

phrases.example: 참 나, 그런 말을 왜 저한테 해요?
phrases.en: Seriously, why are you telling me that?
phrases.nuance_ko: 어이없고 기가 막힐 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are baffled or find something absurd.

phrases.en: Tsk, you shouldn't do that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대를 가볍게 말리거나 못마땅할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to lightly stop someone or show mild disapproval.

explain_en: It comes out first, like talking to yourself, when you are baffled, displeased, or amazed. It is mostly spoken and rarely written. Said to a superior it can sound rude, so use it with close friends or to yourself.

examples.ko: 그거참, 아무도 안 다쳐서 정말 다행이네요.
examples.en: Well, what a relief that nobody got hurt.

examples.ko: 그거참 이상하네요. 어제는 분명히 잘 됐는데요.
examples.en: That's strange. It definitely worked yesterday.
Oh dear, how unfortunate to get sick on the exam day.
Wow, that's amazing. How did you figure it out?
Ah, you prepared so hard, and the result is disappointing.
That's trouble. What should we do now?

explain: 놀람, 아쉬움, 안타까움을 혼잣말처럼 낼 때 써요. 좋은 일에도 나쁜 일에도 쓰고, 말투에 따라 '신기하네'나 '안됐네'처럼 들려요. '거참'이라고 줄여 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: Well, strange things do happen.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그거참'의 줄임말로, 혼잣말이나 편한 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of '그거참', common in muttering or casual talk.

phrases.en: Oh, that's too bad.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그거참'을 줄이지 않은 모양이에요. 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The unshortened form of '그거참'. The meaning is the same.

phrases.en: Wow, that's amazing. How did you know?
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 '신기하네요'를 붙이면 놀라워하는 말이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '신기하네요' after it turns it into an expression of amazement.

explain_en: It is used almost like a muttered reaction to show surprise, regret, or sympathy. It can be used for good or bad news, and depending on tone it sounds like 'how amazing' or 'what a pity'. It can be shortened to '거참'.

t90.ax: That's trouble. What should we do now?

examples.en: Whoa, you can't sit there!
Oops, your umbrella fell on the floor!

examples.ko: 어어, 잠깐만요, 저 아직 안 탔어요!
examples.en: Hey, wait a second, I haven't gotten on yet!

examples.ko: 어어, 이 컴퓨터가 왜 갑자기 꺼지지요?
examples.en: Hey, why is this computer suddenly turning off?
Whoa, it's dangerous if you go that way!
Oh no, the cup is about to tip over!

explain: 갑자기 놀라거나 뭔가 잘못되려고 할 때 급하게 내는 소리예요. 한 번 '어' 하는 것보다 두 번 반복하면 더 다급하고 당황한 느낌이 나요. 보통 뒤에 쉼표를 두고 하려는 말을 이어요.

phrases.en: Whoa, a car is coming!
phrases.nuance_ko: '어어'를 더 길게 끌어서 더 급하고 놀란 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: A drawn-out version that sounds more urgent and startled.

phrases.en: Hey, wait a second! That's mine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무언가를 급하게 멈추게 할 때 뒤에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Added before a request to stop something in a hurry.

phrases.en: Whoa, careful! The floor is slippery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험을 알리며 주의를 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to warn someone of danger and tell them to be careful.

explain_en: Spoken, sudden alarm at something about to fall or go wrong. This is a quick sound you make when you are suddenly startled or something is about to go wrong. Repeating it twice sounds more urgent and flustered than a single '어'. It is usually followed by a comma and then what you want to say.

examples.en: Now now, if you eat that fast you'll get indigestion.
Tut-tut, I told you not to do this.

examples.ko: 어허, 아이 앞에서 그런 말을 하면 어떡해요?
examples.en: Hey now, what are you doing saying that in front of a child?

examples.ko: 어허, 벌써 가려고요? 조금 더 있다 가요.
examples.en: Oh my, you're leaving already? Stay a little longer.
Tsk, are you two fighting again?

examples.ko: 어허, 다 큰 애가 울면 어떡해요?
examples.en: Now now, what are you doing crying when you're all grown up?

explain: 상대를 점잖게 말리거나 타이를 때, 또는 못마땅하거나 놀라울 때 문장 앞에서 내는 소리예요. 어른이 아랫사람에게 말하는 듯한 느낌이 있어서, 친구나 윗사람에게 쓰면 어색할 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 어허, 안 돼요. 그건 만지면 위험해요.
phrases.en: Now now, no. It's dangerous to touch that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점잖게 말릴 때 '어허' 뒤에 '안 돼요'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Eoheo' followed by 'no' to gently stop someone.

phrases.en: Tsk, you're late again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 못마땅하거나 어이없을 때 혼잣말처럼 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said like a mutter when annoyed or exasperated.

phrases.en: Oh dear. The cup broke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안타깝거나 놀라운 일을 봤을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used on seeing something unfortunate or surprising.

explain_en: It is a sound put at the start of a sentence to gently stop or scold someone, or to show disapproval or surprise. It sounds like an older person speaking to someone younger, so it can feel odd when used to friends or superiors.

examples.en: The child runs here and there, so it's chaotic.
I looked all over the place, but there's no key.

examples.ko: 여행 가서 요기조기 구경하며 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: On the trip, I took photos while looking around here and there.
Toys are scattered all over the place.
There's no spot on my body that doesn't hurt.

examples.ko: 요기조기 다니다 보니 하루가 금방 갔어요.
examples.en: Going around here and there, the day passed quickly.

explain: '여기저기'를 귀엽고 친근하게 말하는 구어예요. 아이에게 말하거나 친한 사이에서 쓰고, 글이나 공식적인 자리에서는 '여기저기'라고 해요. 보통 '요기조기 다니다', '요기조기 찾다'처럼 부사처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I looked all over inside the bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요기조기'의 표준적인 말이라서 글이나 공식적인 자리에서도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard form of 'yogijogi', so you can use it in writing and formal settings too.

phrases.en: On the weekend I went around to various places with my child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 곳을 가볍게 돌아다닐 때 귀엽게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cute way to say you went around to many places casually.
phrases.en_equiv: to go around here and there

phrases.en: I looked around the market here and there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한곳에 오래 있지 않고 여러 곳을 가볍게 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you browse many spots lightly without staying long in one place.
phrases.en_equiv: to look around here and there

explain_en: It is a cute, friendly spoken version of '여기저기' (here and there). Use it when talking to children or close friends; in writing or formal settings say '여기저기'. It usually works like an adverb, as in '요기조기 다니다' (go around) or '요기조기 찾다' (look around).

en: trifling like this; a mere ... like this

examples.en: Don't cry over such a small thing.
Rain this light is fine even without an umbrella.
This little homework takes just ten minutes.

examples.ko: 이까짓 돈 때문에 친구랑 싸우지 말아요.
examples.en: Don't fight with your friend over such a little money.

examples.ko: 이까짓 거 혼자서도 충분히 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can do a little thing like this all by myself.
I won't be beaten by a little cold like this.

explain: 눈앞의 일이나 물건을 하찮게 여길 때 쓰는 말투예요. 내가 하는 일에 쓰면 '별거 아니야'라는 오기나 다짐이 되고, 남의 일에 쓰면 무시하는 말로 들릴 수 있어요. 항상 뒤에 명사가 와서 '이까짓 일', '이까짓 거'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 이까짓 거 금방 끝낼 수 있어요.
phrases.en: I can finish a little thing like this in no time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이까짓 것'을 말할 때 줄인 모양으로, 별거 아니라는 가벼운 다짐이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The shortened spoken form of 'this little thing', expressing a casual 'it's nothing'.

phrases.en: A little hardship like this is fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 일을 가볍게 여기며 스스로 힘을 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to shrug off hardship and encourage oneself.

phrases.en: Something like this is nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쯤'이 붙어서 '그 정도는 쉽다'는 느낌이 더 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '쯤' strengthens the feeling of 'that much is easy'.

explain_en: Belittling something right here, near the speaker (이까짓 숙제) This is a tone for belittling something right in front of you. About your own task it sounds like a determined 'no big deal', but about someone else's matter it can sound dismissive. A noun always follows, as in '이까짓 일' or '이까짓 거'.

t90.ax: Don't cry over such a small thing.

examples.en: This food is really delicious.
Thank you so much, you saved me.
The weather is truly nice today.

examples.ko: 그 일이 그렇게 될 줄은 참말 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I truly did not know it would turn out that way.
It has been so long, how have you been?
Is that story true?

explain: '참말'은 '정말'과 거의 같은 뜻이지만 조금 옛날 느낌이 나요. 요즘 대화에서는 '정말', '진짜'를 더 많이 쓰고 참말은 어르신 말투나 글에서 자주 들려요. 명사로 '그 말이 참말이에요?'처럼 '거짓이 아닌 말'로도 써요.

phrases.en: This movie is really fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참말과 같은 뜻이지만 요즘 대화에서 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as 참말 but is used much more in everyday conversation today.

phrases.en: I'm really tired today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가족과 편하게 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is common when talking casually with friends or family.

phrases.en: Is that rumor true?
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사로 쓰여서 거짓이 아닌 말이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a noun, it means words that are not a lie.

explain_en: 참말 means almost the same as 정말, but it feels a little old-fashioned. In everyday talk people say 정말 or 진짜 more, and 참말 is more common in older speakers' talk and in writing. It also works as a noun for words that are not false, as in 그 말이 참말이에요?
